If this is not passed, access to phase 2 is not possible. The monthly gross salary is approximately 2030€ in phase 1 and 2300€ in phase 2 . The Bachelor's degree (or equivalent) must have been obtained after 1 January 2014 . The doctorate must have been obtained after 1 January 2020 . There is one modality, Fullbright , for conducting Phase 1 stays in the United States. The stay must be continuous and last between 20 and 24 months. The following criteria are considered when evaluating applications for Phase 1: - Scientific publications (maximum 40 points). Books with ISBNs and articles receive more points than book chapters. Gross Monthly salary : 1.900,00 € (including the apportionments of extra payments) Expected starting date : 6 March Workday: Full Time (37.5 hours per week) Employment status: Support technician C Place of Work: Pontevedra The Post-Growth Innovation Lab at the University of Vigo invites applications for a research support technitian in the project A Right to a Repair Society: Controversies, Opportunities, and Challenges (ATTRACT) . This project investigates how the Right to Repair (R2R) movement can contribute to a post-growth society while addressing the environmental and social challenges posed by consumer electronics. The full job offer can be found at the following link: https://secretaria.uvigo.gal/uv/web/convocatoria/public/show/1514 (external link) PROJECT OVERVIEW The Right to Repair (R2R) movement advocates for greater rights and collective freedoms to repair our electronic devices, countering manufacturer practices like planned obsolescence. By promoting repairability, R2R aims to reduce electronic waste, limit resource extraction, and foster sustainable consumption practices. This project will map the multiple perspectives surrounding the R2R debate and analyse how these perspectives influence EU legislation on sustainability and circular economy. While mapping out these different perspectives is essential, the project places a strong focus on how they are being integrated in actual R2R legislation, particularly within the European Union. Finally, the project will analyse these dynamics in terms of their alignment with the transition to a post-growth economy. PhD CANDIDATE PROFILE We welcome graduates with a degree in political science, management, international relations or similar. Other merits will be considered: English level C1 or higher Have completed or be in the process of completing a master’s degree related to sustainability and the environment Have completed internships, research or study stays in foreign centres Professional experience in positions related to sustainability, circular economy, climate change or similar, preferably in universities or research centres. Experience in dissemination and organisation of events and activities. Personal interview. The interview will be conducted only with those 5 candidates who, in the sum of the merits, reach a minimum of 50 points HOW TO APPLY The presentation of applications can only be made online via University of Vigo website (https://sede.uvigo.gal/), connecting with an electronic certificate, and entering in "Procedementos" and "Procedementos PAS/PDI" and clicking on the link UCPI 0425- Concurso de méritos para a contratación de persoal investigador . In the subject it must be indicated only the offer reference: OFERTA 0425-146694 Exceptionally for this procedure, only foreigners from outside the European Union will be able to use alternative electronic means of identification, for which they must initiate the procedure by sending an e-mail to estranxeiros@uvigo.gal (external link) . Responsible declaration (Annex I) of fulfillment of the conditions established in the bases of the present call and of the veracity of the data added in the curriculum vitae. ATTRACT Project (Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities) Supervisors : Dr. Javier Lloveras (external link) and Dr. Mario Pansera (external link) Project Title : A Right to a Repair Society: Controversies, Opportunities, and Challenges (ATTRACT) Funding Duration : 4 years Gross salary : approx €23000 per year Scholarship type: Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities Expected starting date : December 2024-January 2025 NEW PRE-APPLICATION DEADLINE : 15 October The Post-Growth Innovation Lab at the University of Vigo invites applications for a fully funded PhD position in the project A Right to a Repair Society: Controversies, Opportunities, and Challenges (ATTRACT) . This project investigates how the Right to Repair (R2R) movement can contribute to a post-growth society while addressing the environmental and social challenges posed by consumer electronics. PROJECT OVERVIEW The Right to Repair (R2R) movement advocates for greater rights and collective freedoms to repair our electronic devices, countering manufacturer practices like planned obsolescence. By promoting repairability, R2R aims to reduce electronic waste, limit resource extraction, and foster sustainable consumption practices. This project will map the multiple perspectives surrounding the R2R debate and analyse how these perspectives influence EU legislation on sustainability and circular economy. While mapping out these different perspectives is essential, the project places a strong focus on how they are being integrated in actual R2R legislation , particularly within the European Union . Finally, the project will analyse these dynamics in terms of their alignment with the transition to a post-growth economy. PhD CANDIDATE PROFILE We welcome applicants from any academic background—be it social sciences, humanities, or natural sciences—as long as they possess the necessary skills and motivations required for the project. Below is a detailed list of the essential skills we are looking for. While it’s not necessary to meet every single criterion, these are the qualities we will prioritize when shortlisting candidates. The ideal candidate will have the following essential skills : A good understanding of the EU legislative process in relevant areas. Experience working with qualitative research methods (e.g., interviews, discourse analysis) and a disposition to develop their qualitative research skills further. Critical thinking and ability to review and synthesize academic literature across various disciplines and fields. Experience conducting systematic literature reviews – or at least, a reasonable understanding of this process. A good understanding of postgrowth/degrowth theories. Availability to travel for fieldwork. Proven ability to carry out academic work in English (writing, reading, and speaking). Ability to communicate in Spanish language is not mandatory but advisable. Autonomy, resilience, and an ability to conduct academic work independently. Teamwork skills and the ability to collaborate effectively. ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS · Candidates must hold a Bachelor's degree, or equivalent, and a Master's degree, or equivalent, provided they have completed at least 300 ECTS credits in the two types of programmes as a whole. · We invited candidates from any discipline to apply. RESPONSIBILITIES To work on a full time PhD whose content will be directly aligned with the general project aim and objectives Conduct a rigorous, systematic review of relevant literature Conduct qualitative research, including aspects of research design, fieldwork, and data analysis. Engage with and collect data from multiple stakeholders in the Right to Repair debate in the EU. From consumer groups to policy makers, to activists and NGOs, etc. Contribute to publications, policy briefs, and public outreach as part of the project. BENEFITS Full funding for 4 years . The opportunity to contribute to innovative research at the intersection of sustainability, postgrowth, and EU policy. Access to international academic and policy networks. Support for career development, including opportunities for publication and participation in international conferences. HOW TO APPLY The application process is divided in two stages (pre-application and formal application). Only shortlisted candidates will be asked to formally apply to the University of Vigo, with detailed instructions provided at that stage. Following the formal application process, interviews will be conducted. Deadline for pre-applications is 15 October . The following documents are required for this pre-application (sent to this e-mail address: postgrowth-lab@uvigo.es (external link) ): Curriculum Vitae (CV) highlighting areas that are relevant to the project A cover letter outlining their research interests and motivation for applying, including how their background fits the project At least one reference letter (preferably two) from relevant referees. A brief research proposal (max. 1,000 words) on how they would approach the PhD topic. The following documents will be later required for the shortlisted applicants invited to make formal application : Abbreviated CV, following the standardized format ( https://cvn.fecyt.es/ (external link) ), with specific emphasis on scientific and technical contributions, as well as international experience and mobility. Academic transcripts. Grading scale and equivalencies (external link) (only for those studies completed outside the Spanish system), formally signed by the issuing institution (external link) . This applies only to foreign degrees. Waterloo campus and city Events GRADimpact stories Grad guide Contact us Resilient urban futures: Connecting practitioners and scholars to reimagine climate adaptation Faculty of Environment Research project description Seeking an interdisciplinary PhD student to examine how foresight and futures-thinking can support municipalities in navigating long-term, equity-oriented urban climate transitions. The student will be embedded within a collaborative research initiative based at the University of Waterloo and will work closely with five municipalities across Canada to explore how participatory and strategic foresight approaches can be used to re-imagine urban futures, guide decision-making under deep uncertainty, and reduce the risk of maladaptation. This research will combine empirical investigation with conceptual development, contributing both to scholarly debates on urban climate governance and to practical tools and insights for municipal practitioners. The accelerating impacts of climate change are placing unprecedented pressures on cities, while also creating space for innovation in governance, planning, and collective action. Canadian municipalities are increasingly on the front-lines of climate mitigation and adaptation, yet they remain constrained by short-term decision-making cycles that clash with the long-term time horizons climate action requires. Because climate impacts unfold over decades and key interventions take years to plan and implement, short-term-ism increases the risk of maladaptation. In addition, addressing climate change demands more than technical solutions; it requires imagination and the ability to envision alternative urban futures. Yet foresight remains unevenly developed at the municipal level in Canada. This project responds by convening municipalities, researchers, and civil society to collectively build foresight capacity. Fields of research Futures studies and strategic foresight Urban climate governance and planning Climate adaptation, mitigation, and resilience Environmental and climate justice Municipal policy and institutional innovation Qualifications and ideal student profile Prospective graduate student researchers must meet or exceed the minimum admission requirements for the programs connected to this opportunity. Visit the program pages using the links on this page to learn more about minimum admission requirements. In addition to minimum requirements, the research supervisor is looking for the following qualifications and student profile. A motivated PhD student with a strong interest in climate change, cities, and foresight methods. The position is particularly well-suited to students interested in research that bridges theory and practice and contributes to real-world climate action. A background in foresight, urban planning, geography, environmental studies, sustainability science, or a related discipline. An interest in climate governance, adaptation, and/or mitigation at the municipal scale Familiarity with, or openness to learning, futures and foresight approaches (e.g., scenario planning, visioning, participatory methods) A collaborative orientation and interest in engaged, practice-facing scholarship Experience working with municipalities, civil society organizations, or participatory research processes is an asset, but not required. Africa , PhD , Scholarships , South America | 0 | Spread the love The University of Bonn and Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences are inviting applications for 10 doctoral research positions under the DFG Research Training Group (RTG) “Urban Future – Managing Transformations for Better Health in Blue Cities.” The interdisciplinary doctoral programme focuses on the relationship between urbanisation, water, public health, ecological sustainability and social justice , with particular attention to cities located along rivers and coastlines. Starting in April 2027 , successful candidates will join a structured four-year doctoral programme that combines individual PhD research with interdisciplinary training, seminars, systems-thinking approaches, transdisciplinary research methods and professional development. The programme is particularly relevant to graduates interested in urban health, public health, climate change, water-health systems, governance, environmental sustainability, infectious diseases, urban planning, ecological systems, development studies and social sciences . Successful doctoral researchers will receive a four-year doctoral support contract with remuneration based on TV-L pay grade 13 (65%) , according to the German public-sector salary scale. Employment will be at either the University of Bonn or Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences. The application deadline is 19 October 2026 . About the Urban Future Research Training Group The DFG Research Training Group “Urban Future” examines how cities can manage urban transformations in ways that improve public health, ecological sustainability and social equity . The programme uses the concept of the “Blue City” to describe urban areas situated along rivers or coastlines where water is considered more than simply a resource or a potential hazard. Instead, water becomes an integral part of: Urban planning Infrastructure development Environmental management Public health Social systems Urban identity Climate adaptation Ecological sustainability The research programme recognises that cities are complex systems in which environmental, social, economic, political and health-related factors interact. Researchers will therefore investigate the connections between urban transformation, water-related challenges and health outcomes , particularly in rapidly changing urban environments. A major emphasis is placed on cities in the Global South , which serve as important living laboratories for understanding urban transformation and developing solutions that can contribute to healthier and more sustainable cities. However, applicants are not restricted to research sites in the Global South. Candidates are free to propose research sites in any Blue City worldwide , provided that the proposed research aligns with the objectives of the programme. Universities and International Research Network The Research Training Group is jointly operated by: University of Bonn Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences It works in cooperation with the German Institute of Development and Sustainability (IDOS) and a network of international partner universities. The international partnership includes institutions in: Ghana Togo Cameroon Brazil Japan The listed partner institutions include: KNUST – Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana University of Ghana, Ghana University of Cape Coast, Ghana University of Lomé, Togo University of Buea, Cameroon University of São Paulo, Brazil The University of Tokyo, Japan This international structure gives doctoral researchers an opportunity to work within a research environment that connects European and Global South perspectives on urban health, sustainability and transformation. Four Research Themes of the Urban Future PhD Programme The doctoral programme is organised around four major interdisciplinary research themes. Research Theme A: Urban Health Resilience The Urban Health Resilience theme examines how urban communities respond to and recover from health pressures associated with water and environmental change. Research may focus on issues such as: Flooding Drought Urban heat islands Air pollution Unequal access to clean water Food systems Environmental exposures Mental health Social inequalities Climate adaptation Green and blue infrastructure The research theme combines perspectives from areas such as epidemiology, sociology, environmental science, urban planning and public health . Researchers will examine how communities can develop greater resilience while ensuring that vulnerable populations are not left behind. Example PhD research topics Potential research areas include: Urban Food Systems Possible methods include: Nutritional analysis Dietary surveys Health outcome measurements Intervention studies Soil Health and Soil Functions Potential methods include: Soil surveys Soil health indicator measurement Ecosystem measurements Functional measurements One Health and Planetary Health Resilience Potential methods include: Human and mental health assessments Environmental exposure measurements Longitudinal studies Spatial analysis Socio-ecological analysis Intervention and transformative studies Urban Blue and Green Infrastructure Potential methods include: Health impact assessments Human and mental health assessments Environmental exposure measurements Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices (KAP) surveys Perception surveys Spatial analysis Ecosystem services accounting Potential supervisors Research Theme A includes supervision from: Prof. Dr. Ina Danquah PD Dr. Timo Falkenberg Prof. Dr. Martin Hamer Prof. Wiltrud Terlau Prof. Dr. Mariele Evers Research Theme B: Urban Disease Ecology The Urban Disease Ecology theme explores how environmental and ecological conditions in urban water landscapes affect disease transmission and human health. The theme is particularly concerned with: Water-borne diseases Vector-borne diseases Infectious diseases Climate-related health risks Water quality Urban morphology Land-use changes Urban density Pathogen transmission Antimicrobial resistance The research takes a One Health approach, recognising the interconnected relationship between human health, animals and the environment. Researchers may investigate how changes in urban development, water management and environmental conditions affect the spread of infectious diseases. Example PhD research topics Antimicrobial Resistance Possible methods include: Microbiological sampling Cultural analysis Molecular analysis Resistance profiling Surveys Water quality analysis Transmission modelling Impact modelling Helminth Infections and Non-Communicable Diseases Potential methods include: Parasitological analysis Microbiological analysis Immunological analysis Clinical examinations Biomarker analysis Mouse models for mechanistic research Urban Microbiome and Dietary Ecology Potential methods include: Microbiome sequencing Dietary pattern analysis Metagenomic analysis Computational analysis Vector-Borne Disease Potential methods include: Climate monitoring Entomological surveys Temperature mapping Vector modelling Pathogen detection Potential supervisors Research Theme B includes: Prof. Dr. Christian Borgemeister Prof. Dr. Achim Hörauf Prof. Dr. Marc Hübner Dr. Indulekha Karunakaran Prof. Dr. Nico Mutters PD Dr. Marijo Parcina Dr. Manuel Ritter Prof. Dr. Marie-Christine Simon Dr. Nicole Zacharias Research Theme C: Governance and Institutional Change The Governance and Institutional Change theme is particularly relevant to applicants interested in policy, governance, economics, development studies, political science, institutional systems and public-sector transformation. This research theme examines how political, institutional and societal structures influence urban transformation and the ability of cities to respond to health and environmental challenges. Areas of interest include: Urban governance Water-health governance Public policy Institutional design Policy instruments Inter-sectoral collaboration Financing mechanisms Participatory decision-making Climate adaptation Population growth Unequal resource distribution Political economy Technological change Healthcare policy Institutional transformation The research seeks to generate evidence that can support more inclusive, transparent and adaptive approaches to urban development . Example PhD research topics Biodiversity-Based Bio-Economies Possible methods include: Economic impact assessment Policy analysis Value-chain analysis Cross-Sectoral Governance Potential methods include: Stakeholder mapping Policy analysis Governance framework development Case studies Urban Transformation and Pharmaceutical Innovation Potential methods include: Case study analysis Technology assessment Policy evaluation Innovation studies Political Economy of Health Equity and Technological Change Potential methods include: Political economy analysis Institutional economics Policy process tracing Case studies Impact analysis Urban Healthcare Policy Implementation Potential methods include: Institutional economics Case studies Impact analysis Microeconometric evaluation Climate-Responsive Health Policy Potential methods include: Policy mapping Infrastructure mapping Spatial analysis Policy evaluation Implementation research Economic impact assessment Potential supervisors Research Theme C includes: Prof. Dr. Katja Bender Prof. Dr. Jan Börner Prof. Dr. Anna-Katharina Hornidge Prof. Dr. Simona Helmsmüller Dr. Christoph Strupat Research Theme D: Adaptive Urban Ecosystems The Adaptive Urban Ecosystems theme focuses on how cities can plan and manage ecological and blue-green infrastructure in response to climate change and socio-economic transformation. Research areas include: Urban land-use systems Water infrastructure Nature-based solutions Ecosystem resilience Climate adaptation Circular economy Integrated water-resource management Biodiversity Urban soil management Ecosystem services Sustainable urban development This theme brings together engineering, ecological and planning perspectives to investigate how urban environments can be designed to provide multiple benefits for both people and ecosystems. Example PhD research topics Coupling Mechanisms of Urbanization Potential methods include: Hydrological modelling System-dynamics modelling Ecosystem-services analysis Biodiversity and Human Wellbeing Potential methods include: Biodiversity surveys Spatial data analysis Socioeconomic surveys Urban Soil Management Potential methods include: Soil sampling Soil biodiversity surveys Morphological identification Molecular identification Soil health indicators Spatial analysis Urban Decision Environments Potential methods include: Coupled ecological-economic systems modelling Collective learning dynamics One Planetary Health Potential methods include: Integrated modelling Framework development Systems thinking Commons governance studies Potential supervisors Research Theme D includes: Prof. Dr. Wolfram Barfuss Dr. Bibiana Betancur Prof. Dr. Lisa Biber-Freudenberger Prof. Dr. Mariele Evers What Does the PhD Programme Offer? Successful candidates will receive a structured doctoral research experience rather than simply conducting an independent PhD project. The programme provides several forms of academic and professional support. 1. Four-Year Doctoral Support Contract The Research Training Group will begin on 1 April 2027 . Successful applicants will receive a four-year doctoral support contract , with remuneration dependent on TV-L pay grade 13 at 65% , in accordance with the German public salary scale. Employment will be at either: University of Bonn; or Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences. 2. Funded Research Expenses The programme states that fieldwork, travel and related research expenses are fully funded . This is particularly important for doctoral projects involving international fieldwork or research in different urban environments. 3. Structured Doctoral Training Doctoral researchers will participate in an interdisciplinary training programme covering areas such as: Systems thinking Transdisciplinary research Academic communication Interdisciplinary research Research methods Soft skills Professional development 4. Interdisciplinary Research Environment The programme brings together researchers from different academic disciplines. This allows doctoral candidates to examine urban health challenges from multiple perspectives rather than approaching them from a single discipline. 5. International Research Network Researchers will have access to a strong national and international network involving universities and research institutions in Europe, Africa, Asia and Latin America. 6. Career Development Support The programme also provides dedicated career development support , structured supervision and clear progression criteria. Responsibilities of Selected Doctoral Researchers Successful candidates will be expected to actively participate in the Research Training Group and contribute to its interdisciplinary research environment. Their responsibilities will include: Participating actively in the RTG training programme. Taking part in interdisciplinary seminars. Conducting independent doctoral research aligned with one of the four research themes. Developing appropriate research methodologies. Collecting and analysing research data. Publishing research findings. Contributing to the development of Blue City concepts. Participating in transdisciplinary knowledge exchange. Developing systems-thinking and interdisciplinary research capabilities. Who Can Apply? The programme is seeking applicants who have already completed a Master’s degree or equivalent qualification in a relevant discipline. The call specifically identifies a broad range of eligible academic backgrounds. These include: Agricultural and Food Systems Climate and Earth Sciences Development Studies Ecology and Life Sciences Economics and Management Mathematics Physics Computer Science Environmental Sciences Health Sciences Geography Infectious Diseases Hygiene and Infection Control Medical Microbiology Public Health Urban and Regional Studies Social Sciences Applicants should also demonstrate: A strong interdisciplinary mindset A clear interest in urban transformation Interest in the water-health nexus and/or urban health Excellent written English Excellent spoken English English Language Requirement Applicants are required to provide evidence of English language proficiency at B2 level , according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR), or an equivalent qualification such as TOEFL. Is the Opportunity Open to International Applicants? Yes. The programme has an explicitly international research orientation and involves partner institutions across Africa, Asia, Latin America and Europe . The call identifies partner institutions in Ghana, Togo, Cameroon, Brazil and Japan , while applicants are permitted to propose research sites in any Blue City worldwide . Therefore, the programme is not presented as being restricted to German or European applicants. Applicants should, however, ensure that they satisfy the academic, language and application requirements specified in the official call. Application Documents Required The application process consists of two stages . Applications will first be assessed by the RTG Selection Committee. Candidates considered among the most qualified will then be invited to participate in a virtual interview . Applicants are required to submit the following: 1. Curriculum Vitae A tabular-format CV should be provided, presenting the applicant’s academic background, professional experience, research experience, skills and other relevant information. 2. Degree Certificates and Transcripts Applicants must provide: Higher education degree certificate(s) Full transcript(s) of records An explanation of the grading system used for previous studies 3. Motivation Letter A motivation letter of no more than 500 words is required. The letter should explain the applicant’s motivation for joining the programme and demonstrate their interest in the relevant research area. 4. Research Exposé Applicants must submit a research exposé of no more than 1,500 words . This is an important part of the application because candidates are expected to propose doctoral research aligned with one of the programme’s four research themes. 5. Interdisciplinary Research Statement Applicants must provide an interdisciplinary research statement of no more than 500 words . This should demonstrate their ability to think across disciplinary boundaries and connect their proposed research with the wider objectives of the Research Training Group. 6. Letter of Recommendation Applicants must submit one letter of recommendation . 7. English Language Certificate Applicants must provide evidence of B2-level English proficiency , such as CEFR, TOEFL or an equivalent qualification. Application Deadline The deadline to submit a complete application is: 19 October 2026 Applicants should ensure that all required documents are prepared and submitted through the online application portal before the deadline. Candidates should also indicate the specific research theme they are applying for. Important Information About Gender Equality The call states that, in accordance with the Landesgleichstellungsgesetz (LGG) NRW , women will be given preference in cases where candidates have equal suitability, qualifications and professional performance, unless reasons relating to another candidate prevail. The programme also states that it is committed to diversity and equal opportunity and is certified as a family-friendly university . Why the Blue City Concept Matters The Blue City concept is central to the programme. Rather than treating water solely as something that cities need to control, remove or supply, the programme examines water as an important component of the urban environment. This approach can involve examining: Rivers Coastlines Flood management Water infrastructure Public health Urban ecosystems Climate resilience Green-blue infrastructure Water quality Urban planning Social equity Disease ecology Governance The programme therefore recognises that water-related challenges cannot always be addressed through engineering solutions alone. They may also require changes in governance, public policy, community participation, health systems, environmental management and urban planning. why_it_matches: This MSCA Doctoral Position investigates the social and organizational implications of individual AI-augmentation, focusing on how personalized AI routines affect collaboration, oversight, and organizational resilience. This aligns well with the candidate's interests in social practices, systemic design, governance, policy, and social transformation. The project's emphasis on qualitative and mixed-method research, examining power, control, and culture within organizations, directly matches the candidate's methodological comfort and expertise. While the core subject is AI, the sociological and STS framing of the research avoids the technical AI focus the candidate wishes to avoid, instead concentrating on human agency and organizational dynamics.
strategic_fit: The project contributes to understanding the evolving nature of work and organizational systems in the digital age, which can be linked to broader discussions around consumption systems and social transformation, albeit not directly in a degrowth context. The focus on governance and policy around emerging technologies is also a strong strategic fit.

title: PhD scholarship in Auditing
why_it_matches: The PhD offers a specific research theme on 'the role of auditing and assurance in sustainable development,' encouraging exploration of alternative forms of auditing beyond compliance and aiming for a meaningful role in sustainability. This aligns well with the candidate's strong interest in sustainable consumption, ecological/social transformation, and systemic design. The call welcomes applicants from other social sciences interested in auditing as a research domain, which suits the candidate's background in design research, sustainability education, and openness to fields like sociology or political science. The preference for qualitative research methods is also a strong match.
strategic_fit: This position offers a unique opportunity to apply systemic and critical thinking to the often-overlooked domain of auditing within the context of sustainable development. It directly addresses the candidate's interest in sustainable consumption and systems by challenging traditional compliance-oriented approaches and seeking transformative roles for assurance in sustainability. While not explicitly degrowth, the focus on 'alternative forms' and 'meaningful role' beyond current models resonates with the candidate's trajectory towards post-growth and social transformation. The project's engagement with 'evolving societal demands' and 'debate about how auditing and assurance can play a meaningful role in sustainability' aligns with interests in governance and policy.
why_it_is_not_perfect: The core discipline of 'Auditing' and 'Accounting' is quite distant from the candidate's primary background in Industrial Design and Service Design. While the candidate is open to non-design fields, the direct connection to design methodologies or theories might be limited unless the project can be creatively framed. The terms 'degrowth,' 'post-growth,' 'alternative ownership/access,' or 'commons' are not explicitly mentioned, requiring the candidate to frame their proposal to connect these interests to the auditing context. One of the research themes also mentions 'generative artificial intelligence,' which the candidate aims to avoid, though it's not the central focus of the entire call.

title: PhD position in Economic Ethics and/or Environmental Ethics (Financial Ethics Research Group / Sustainable Finance Lab)
university: University of Gothenburg, Department of Philosophy, Linguistics and Theory of Science
funding: PhD position in Sweden, funded as full-time employment for four years, with salary, occupational pension, 28 days base vacation, wellness time during working hours and compensation for medical visits. Connected to the Vinnova-funded Sustainable Finance Lab research programme.
why_it_matches: The research area is deliberately broad and includes the political philosophy of markets, ethics of commodification, consumer duties to buy or invest sustainably, firm and bank duties to mitigate climate change, collective action problems and the philosophy of environmental economics — all of which touch the candidate's ownership/access, consumption, political-economy and post-growth interests from a normative angle. It is a theoretical, argument-driven PhD, matching her comfort with theoretical and critical work, and it values a self-formulated research question, which suits a design researcher used to framing problems. Deductions: low design compatibility, a philosophy department where applicants normally need a demonstrable philosophical research background, and an ethics rather than systems/practice framing of sustainability. Included nevertheless as a genuinely funded, clearly specified, future-deadline vacancy with meaningful overlap on markets, commodities and sustainable consumption.
strategic_fit: Extends the trajectory from design-based sustainability research into normative political economy, providing the theoretical/philosophical grounding for sufficiency, limitarianism, commons and degrowth arguments that the candidate currently approaches through design and social practice. The Financial Ethics Research Group and Sustainable Finance Lab connect this work to markets, money and institutional reform, supporting the social and political transformation strand of her agenda.
